top_stories.title: Inside the fight over Claude Mythos 5
top_stories.summary: Anthropic is in a standoff with the White House over export controls on its Claude Mythos 5 model, with the Trump administration seeking restrictions that Anthropic is resisting. The dispute centres on how the model can be deployed internationally and what sovereign AI arrangements are permissible. The Verge reports the conflict is ongoing and has broader implications for US AI export policy.

top_stories.title: Anthropic Is Still at Odds With the White House Over Claude Fable 5 [Metered]
top_stories.summary: Wired reports that Anthropic remains in dispute with the White House over export controls affecting its next-generation Claude model, referred to as both Fable 5 and Mythos. The disagreement involves whether the administration can restrict where and how the model is deployed globally. The standoff has drawn attention to tensions between AI companies and government oversight of frontier models.

top_stories.title: DOJ Lawyers Argue xAI Is 'Vital' for National Security in NAACP Lawsuit [Metered]
top_stories.summary: US Department of Justice lawyers have intervened in an NAACP lawsuit against xAI, arguing that Elon Musk's AI company is vital to national security. The move signals the federal government's willingness to shield AI firms from civil litigation on national security grounds. The case raises significant questions about AI ethics, bias accountability, and the limits of government protection for AI companies.

top_stories.title: Meta's chaotic AI strategy [Metered]
top_stories.summary: Wired reports on internal turmoil at Meta following a major AI reorganisation, with CTO Andrew Bosworth acknowledging the restructuring was 'atrocious'. Employees have expressed significant unrest over the changes, which were intended to consolidate Meta's AI efforts. The account highlights the difficulties large technology companies face in managing rapid AI-driven organisational change.

top_stories.title: Microsoft turns to AWS as GitHub faces AI capacity crunch
top_stories.summary: Microsoft has reportedly turned to Amazon Web Services to handle overflow demand as GitHub struggles with an AI capacity crunch, according to RuntimeWire. The move underscores the intense pressure on AI compute infrastructure as developer adoption of AI coding tools accelerates. It also highlights the complex interdependencies forming between major cloud and AI platform providers.

further_links.title: Trump's Anthropic shutdown just made the case for non-American AI
further_links.summary: The Verge argues that the US government's pressure on Anthropic over Claude export controls may accelerate international efforts to develop sovereign AI models outside American jurisdiction.

further_links.title: Import AI 461: 'Alignment is not on track'; FrontierCode; and synthetic research interns
further_links.summary: Jack Clark's Import AI newsletter covers concerns that AI alignment research is falling behind capabilities, alongside updates on frontier coding benchmarks and the use of synthetic AI agents as research assistants.

further_links.title: Facebook's new AI Mode search gets its info from public posts
further_links.summary: Meta has launched an AI Mode for Facebook search that surfaces answers drawn from public posts on the platform, raising questions about accuracy and content sourcing.

further_links.title: Meta Tapped a Pentagon Supplier to Prototype Face Recognition for Its Glasses [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired reports that Meta worked with a Pentagon-linked supplier to prototype facial recognition capabilities for its Ray-Ban smart glasses, raising significant privacy and ethics concerns.

further_links.title: Big Tech's desperate last push at AI regulation
further_links.summary: The Verge examines technology industry lobbying efforts in Congress around AI regulation, including child safety legislation, as the policy window for federal AI rules narrows.

further_links.title: Why do South Koreans love AI so much? [Metered]
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review explores South Korea's unusually high public enthusiasm for AI adoption, examining cultural, economic, and policy factors that distinguish the country from other major markets.

further_links.title: Can Europe train a frontier AI model on the compute it owns?
further_links.summary: A GitHub-hosted analysis examines whether Europe has sufficient sovereign compute capacity to train a competitive frontier AI model, assessing current infrastructure against the scale required.

further_links.title: Skydio CEO Adam Bry on why Silicon Valley shouldn't draw red lines for drone use
further_links.summary: Skydio's CEO argues that technology companies should not unilaterally restrict military applications of autonomous drones, pushing back against ethical red lines drawn by some in the tech industry.

further_links.title: This man with ALS is 'the first power user' of a brain implant that lets him speak [Metered]
further_links.summary: MIT Technology Review profiles a patient with ALS who has become an advanced user of a brain-computer interface, using the implant to communicate fluidly in a significant milestone for BCI technology.

further_links.title: The Jqwik Anti-AI Affair
further_links.summary: The maintainer of the Jqwik open-source Java testing library writes about the decision to add an anti-AI policy to the project, sparking debate about AI-generated contributions and open-source governance.
